title: PM Fils-Aimé Announces Official Diplomatic Mission to Rome and the Vatican, May 8–11
detail: Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé announced on May 7, 2026 that he will lead a high-level government delegation on an official diplomatic mission to Rome and the Vatican from May 8–11, 2026. The specific agenda items were not publicly disclosed in available sources, but the visit is expected to include meetings with Holy See officials and potentially Italian government counterparts. The Vatican maintains a significant institutional presence in Haiti through the Catholic Church, which operates schools, hospitals, and humanitarian programs throughout the crisis. The visit follows Fils-Aimé's consolidation of executive authority on February 7, 2026, and his high-profile CNN/Amanpour interview on May 1, 2026, in which he outlined the three-part security strategy — Force, Justice, and Reinsertion — and expressed 'cautious optimism' about a reduction in gang control of Port-au-Prince from approximately 90% to approximately 75%. The Rome and Vatican mission represents Fils-Aimé's latest effort to build international political support and potentially mobilize additional humanitarian, development, and diplomatic resources through faith-based institutional networks. It also signals Haiti's outreach to European political centers as the GSF build-up progresses and international donors are pressed to close the approximately $708 million gap in the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan.

media.caption: PM Fils-Aimé announces official diplomatic mission to Rome and the Vatican, May 8–11, 2026, to build international support for Haiti's stabilization

title: Haitian Ministry Requests PNH and FAd'H Security for Quarry Operations Under Gang Extortion Threat
detail: A Haitian ministry formally requested security assistance from both the Haitian National Police (PNH) and the Armed Forces of Haiti (FAd'H) on May 7, 2026 to protect active quarry and extractive operations from gang interference and extortion. The request reflects the continued spread of gang criminality beyond urban residential zones into the productive infrastructure sector — quarries providing construction and infrastructure materials are increasingly being targeted as gangs seek to control logistics networks, impose extortion 'taxes' on commercial operations, and disrupt economic activity as a leverage tool against both businesses and the state. The formal request also highlights the operational strain on the PNH and FAd'H, both of which are simultaneously supporting GSF joint operations in Port-au-Prince while being asked to extend security coverage to rural and semi-rural economic sites that gangs have penetrated. The request is consistent with the ACLED and ICG-documented pattern of gang extortion expanding into a structural parallel economy generating an estimated $100–400 million annually. Security analysts note that protecting quarry operations requires sustained presence in areas with difficult terrain where gangs operate with impunity — a persistent challenge while the full 5,500-person GSF will not reach operational density until fall–end 2026.

media.caption: Haitian ministry requests PNH and FAd'H security protection for quarry operations as gang extortion spreads to the extractive sector
